knowledge:
- key_parameters: layout=Controls the visual arrangement of multiple motifs (e.g., "stack", "tree", "radialPhylog", "rectangles") ;; ic.scale=Logical indicating whether to scale character heights by information content (default TRUE; set to FALSE for probability/same height) ;; markers=A list of marker objects ("rect", "line", "text") to annotate specific positions on the logo ;; reorder=Logical indicating whether to reorder the input motifs in motifStack (default TRUE; set to FALSE to preserve input order) ;; motifScale=Scale of the motifs in radial/circos/pile plots, e.g., "logarithmic"
- alternatives: seqlogo=A tool for individual sequence logos, but lacks the ability to depict relationships among multiple motifs ;; MotIV::motifDistances=Previously used for calculating motif distances (STAMP implementation) but dropped from Bioconductor; motifStack now uses an R implementation of matalign by default
- when_to_use: Use when visualizing transcription factor binding site motifs, RNA motifs, amino acid sequence conservation, or position-specific affinity matrices (PSAMs), especially when comparing multiple motifs and displaying their relationships via hierarchical clustering, radial trees, or circos layouts.
- pitfalls: Failing to match the row names of the input matrix to the alphabet (e.g., "A", "C", "G", "T" for DNA; "A", "C", "G", "U" for RNA; 20 amino acids for proteins) which will cause errors in S4 class initialization ;; Using the deprecated MotIV package for distance calculations instead of the default clusterMotifs or matalign ;; SVG generation warnings when Cairo graphics are not properly configured or when using non-Cairo generated SVGs.

workflows.name: single_motif_logo
workflows.intent: Import a single position count/frequency/affinity matrix and plot it as a customized sequence or affinity logo with markers and custom styles.
input: motif_matrix.txt (A text file containing a position count matrix (PCM), position frequency matrix (PFM), or position-specific affinity matrix (PSAM) with rows representing bases/amino acids and columns representing positions)
workflows.stages: 1. Import matrix using importMatrix or read raw table ;; 2. Convert/create S4 object (new("pcm"), new("pfm"), or new("psam")) ;; 3. Define markers (new("marker")) ;; 4. Plot using plot()
workflows.code:
pcm <- read.table(file.path(find.package("motifStack"), "extdata", "bin_SOLEXA.pcm"))
pcm <- pcm[,3:ncol(pcm)]
rownames(pcm) <- c("A","C","G","T")
motif <- new("pcm", mat=as.matrix(pcm), name="bin_SOLEXA")
plot(motif)
plot(motif, ic.scale=FALSE, ylab="probability")
motif@color <- colorset(colorScheme='basepairing')
plot(motif,font="serif")
markerRect <- new("marker", type="rect", start=6, stop=7, gp=gpar(lty=2, fill=NA, col="orange"))
markerLine <- new("marker", type="line", start=2, stop=7, gp=gpar(lwd=2, col="red"))
markerText <- new("marker", type="text", start=c(1, 5), label=c("*", "core"), gp=gpar(cex=2, col="red"))
motif <- new("pcm", mat=as.matrix(pcm), name="bin_SOLEXA", markers=c(markerRect, markerLine, markerText))
plot(motif)
plot(motif, xaxis=paste0("pos", seq.int(7)+10))
rna <- pcm
rownames(rna)[4] <- "U"
motif <- new("pcm", mat=as.matrix(rna), name="RNA_motif")
plot(motif)

workflows.name: multiple_motif_stack_tree
workflows.intent: Align, cluster, and plot multiple motifs in a vertical stack, hierarchical tree, or radial phylogeny.
input: motif_folder/ (A directory containing multiple PCM/PFM files in formats like .jaspar, .meme, .transfac, .scpd, .cisbp, or .psam)
workflows.stages: 1. Import multiple matrices ;; 2. (Optional) Convert DNA to RNA motifs using DNAmotifToRNAmotif ;; 3. Plot using motifStack with layout "stack", "tree", or "radialPhylog"
workflows.code:
motifs<-importMatrix(dir(file.path(find.package("motifStack"), "extdata"),"pcm$", full.names = TRUE))
motifStack(motifs, layout="stack", ncex=1.0)
rnaMotifs <- DNAmotifToRNAmotif(motifs)
motifStack(rnaMotifs, layout = "stack", reorder=FALSE)
motifStack(motifs, layout="tree")

workflows.name: advanced_grouped_motif_layouts
workflows.intent: Cluster multiple motifs, extract signatures, and plot them using advanced layouts like tag clouds, circos plots, pile heatmaps, or interactive D3.js plots.
input: pfm_list.rds (An R list object containing multiple PFM objects or a directory of motif matrices)
workflows.stages: 1. Cluster motifs using clusterMotifs ;; 2. Convert hclust to phylog using ade4::hclust2phylog ;; 3. Extract signatures using motifSignature ;; 4. Plot using motifCloud, plotMotifStackWithRadialPhylog, motifCircos, motifPiles, or browseMotifs
workflows.code:
motifs2 <- mapply(pfms, names(pfms), FUN=function(.ele, .name){ new("pfm",mat=.ele, name=.name)}, SIMPLIFY = FALSE)
motifs2 <- lapply(motifs2, trimMotif, t=0.4)
motifStack(motifs2, layout="radialPhylog", circle=0.3, cleaves = 0.2, clabel.leaves = 0.5, col.bg=rep(color, each=3), col.bg.alpha=0.3, col.leaves=rep(color, each=3), col.inner.label.circle=rep(color, each=3), inner.label.circle.width=0.05, col.outer.label.circle=rep(color, each=3), outer.label.circle.width=0.02, circle.motif=1.2, angle=350)
hc <- clusterMotifs(pfms)
library(ade4)
phylog <- ade4::hclust2phylog(hc)
leaves <- names(phylog$leaves)
pfms <- pfms[leaves]
motifSig <- motifSignature(pfms, phylog, cutoffPval=0.0001, min.freq=1)
motifCloud(motifSig, scale=c(6, .5), layout="rectangles", group.col=group.col, groups=groups, draw.legend=TRUE)
sig <- signatures(motifSig)
gpCol <- sigColor(motifSig)
plotMotifStackWithRadialPhylog(phylog=phylog, pfms=sig, circle=0.4, cleaves = 0.3, clabel.leaves = 0.5, col.bg=rep(color, each=3), col.bg.alpha=0.3, col.leaves=rep(rev(color), each=3), col.inner.label.circle=gpCol, inner.label.circle.width=0.03, angle=350, circle.motif=1.2, motifScale="logarithmic")
motifCircos(phylog=phylog, pfms=pfms, pfms2=sig, col.tree.bg=rep(color, each=5), col.tree.bg.alpha=0.3, col.leaves=rep(rev(color), each=5), col.inner.label.circle=gpCol, inner.label.circle.width=0.03, col.outer.label.circle=gpCol, outer.label.circle.width=0.03, r.rings=c(0.02, 0.03, 0.04), col.rings=list(sample(colors(), 30), sample(colors(), 30), sample(colors(), 30)), angle=350, motifScale="logarithmic")
pfmsAligned <- DNAmotifAlignment(pfms)
motifPiles(phylog=phylog, pfms=pfmsAligned, col.tree=rep(color, each=5), col.leaves=rep(rev(color), each=5), col.pfms2=gpCol, r.anno=rep(0.02, length(dl)), col.anno=dl, motifScale="logarithmic", plotIndex=TRUE, groupDistance=10)
browseMotifs(pfms = pfms, phylog = phylog, layout="tree", yaxis = FALSE, baseWidth=6, baseHeight = 15)

workflows.name: ggplot2_motif_plotting
workflows.intent: Plot motifs within a ggplot2 framework using geom_motif.
input: pfm_object.rds (An R object containing a PFM or PCM motif)
workflows.stages: 1. Create data frame with coordinates and motif list ;; 2. Plot using ggplot + geom_motif()
workflows.code:
df <- data.frame(xmin=c(.25, .25), ymin=c(.25, .75), xmax=c(.75, .75), ymax=c(.5, 1), fontfamily=c("serif", "mono"), fontface=c(2, 1))
df$motif <- list(pfm, pfm)
library(ggplot2)
ggplot(df, aes(xmin=xmin, ymin=ymin, xmax=xmax, ymax=ymax, motif=motif, fontfamily=fontfamily, fontface=fontface)) + geom_motif() + theme_bw() + ylim(0, 1) + xlim(0, 1)
df <- data.frame(x=.5, y=c(.25, .75), width=.5, height=.25, fontfamily=c("serif", "mono"), fontface=c(2, 1))
df$motif <- list(pfm, pfm)
ggplot(df, aes(x=x, y=y, width=width, height=height, motif=motif, fontfamily=fontfamily, fontface=fontface)) + geom_motif(use.xy=TRUE) + theme_bw() + ylim(0, 1) + xlim(0, 1)
